sections.heading: Java Anonymous Class
paragraphs: An anonymous class in Java is an inner class which is declared without any class name at all. In other words, a nameless inner class in Java is called an anonymous inner class. Since it does not have a name, it cannot have a constructor because we know that a constructor name is the same as the class name.

sections.heading: Use of Java Anonymous Inner Classes
paragraphs: Anonymous inner classes are used when you want to create a simple class that is needed for one time only for a specific purpose. For example, implementing an interface or extending a class.

sections.heading: Defining Anonymous Class in Java
